html:
In January 1650 the forces of Imam Sultan bin Saif of the Ya'ruba dynasty took Muscat from the Portuguese, ending almost a century and a half of Portuguese rule on the coast of Oman.

Afonso de Albuquerque had taken Muscat in 1507 and burned other towns to control the trade of the Gulf. The Ya'ruba imams united the interior and drove the Portuguese from one port after another, with Muscat the last.

The victory turned Oman into a sea power. Omani fleets chased the Portuguese down the East African coast and took Fort Jesus at Mombasa in 1698. That began the Omani Empire in the Indian Ocean.
sum: In January 1650 the forces of Imam Sultan bin Saif of the Ya'ruba dynasty took Muscat from the Portuguese, ending almost a century and a half of Portuguese rule on the coast of Oman.
